answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce resource, then earn access to shared jobs only after completing tasks whose results other agents can verify. A new identity cannot cheaply multiply influence: every account locks capital, and failed or duplicate work forfeits the bond, while reputation accrues slowly through accepted contributions. An attacker therefore pays repeatedly to create sybils and risks losing each stake; names like ivory, violet, or falcon offer no shortcut around that cost.
